answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so leaving primary uncovered raises delivery risk. Deferral (c5) was only shown on non-critical month-to-month; a second source does not replace the expiring primary. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiation is unlikely to deliver the 18% cut this cycle. Switching may cut unit cost (c2) but a new primary in 14 days with no buffer would increase delivery risk and violate the hard constraint. Renewing keeps integration and deliveries stable (c1). Verifying c1 and c2 to check renewal stability versus actual onboarding speed before lock-in; cost-cut path remains unproven under this timeline.
